new_statements.rule_in_words: The only accessible primary descriptions (Santandrea 1963, 1964) treat Kare as a tone language with three levels (high, low, mid) and mark tone only sporadically; neither says anything about word stress or accent placement. No stress rule can be stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the 1964 note adds that some 3rd-person possessive forms 'differ only in tone' and that one tonal observation is 'a rather poor foundation to build any theory upon' (Santandrea 1964: ca. 105-106).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone marking on wordlist citation forms (Kare A and Kare B varieties of the South Sudan remnant groups). Nothing on stress at word or phrase level.
new_statements.identity_note: Santandrea's 'Kare' is the remnant Kare population of Western Bahr el Ghazal (South Sudan), which he splits into 'Kare A' and 'Kare B' varieties (Kare B has mj where Kare A has nz, etc.); Glottolog links both Santandrea articles to kari1306, the Congolese Bantu Kari/Kare (Guthrie D.301) also recorded by Dijkmans 1927-1947 as the 'restvolk Kare'. Glottolog 5.3 classifies it as Bantu (Ngombe-Ababuan > Ababuan > Old Bomokandian > Ngbele-Ngenda), not Ubangian. The Glottolog-linked Enfield 2005 sketch is a different language (Kri/Kàrì, Vietic, Laos).

new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is given. The note treats Kare as having lexical/grammatical tone (possessive forms 'differ only in tone'; a pronoun vowel 'with a definite high tone') and says nothing at all about stress, accent, prominence or syllable weight. Full-volume scanned searches for stress / stressed / accent / pitch / intonation / prominence / syllable / penultimate return no hit inside the Kare note; the only 'stress' hits in vol. 45 are in Stevenson's Nuba Mountains paper, Asad's Kababish paper and a review.
new_statements.exceptions: none on stress; Santandrea himself calls the tone observation 'a rather poor foundation to build any theory upon'
new_statements.identity_note: Santandrea distinguishes two varieties, Kare A and Kare B, of the Kare remnant in the Bahr el Ghazal (South Sudan); the 1964 paradigms are labelled 'from KARE A'. Glottolog files both Santandrea papers under kari1306 (Kari, Bantu C, DR Congo). Enfield 2005 'Sketch of Kàrì, a Vietic language of Laos' is mis-linked in Glottolog to this code and is not about this language. Dijkmans 1974 Kare-taal (Dutch wordlist, HathiTrust search-only, Google Books no preview) was not among the listed works and remains unopened.

new_statements.identity_note: Santandrea's 'Kare' is the Bantu remnant language of the western Bahr el Ghazal (Raga / Deim Zubeir area, South Sudan), with two sections he calls Kare A and Kare B; Glottolog files both articles (refs 106698, 121557) under kari1306 Kari (Bomokandian > Ngbele-Ngenda).
